title: Module manifest and feature policy contracts

independence.cross_vendor_exception: Not satisfied: every assigned run is Anthropic claude-opus-5. The Decision Register permits a single-vendor fallback only as an explicit recorded exception. Five separate runs with distinct capability declarations, none reviewing its own work, is that fallback. It is not equivalent to cross-vendor review, and runs sharing a vendor and a model share a correlated blind spot.

required_human_authorities: Product Owner disposition of RFC-2026-004 before the manual merge described in RFC-2026-002
purpose: Materialize CTR-MOD-001 and CTR-FLG-001 from the Sprint 0A baseline as schema plus synthetic fixtures, taking every rule from a named workstream task and declaring in-schema which task each rule comes from. These are the two contracts the composition root and the policy router depend on, so their deny-by-default and precedence rules are materialized rather than described.

include: CTR-MOD-001 schema, manifest and synthetic fixtures: MR-001 rejection rules, MR-004 deny-by-default activation, MR-005 lifecycle states
CTR-FLG-001 schema, manifest and synthetic fixtures: FP-001 reason and source, FP-002 precedence and kill switch, FP-003 allocation, FP-005 expiry and owner
An x-source annotation on every rule naming the baseline task it comes from
An untestable_by_fixture declaration on both manifests for the properties a single document cannot demonstrate
exclude: Contract freeze-level advancement, contract-catalog/shared-kernel/index.json, the registry resolution algorithm, the dependency resolver, the bucket allocation algorithm, the circuit-state machine, admin APIs, production schema, migrations, provider SDKs, credentials, customer data, network calls, Gate G0 approval and any merge authorization

contracts_produced: CTR-MOD-001 and CTR-FLG-001 materialized at Draft only; no freeze-level advancement

authorized_cross_package_amendments: test-kits/integrity-manifest.json — add this package's new test file and recompute digests. The WP-0A-A0-002 guard REQUIRES every discovered test file to be digested (exit 87), so any package adding a suite must touch that file. This is a structural coupling created by that guard, not a discretionary edit: the alternative is that the package cannot ship a test at all. It changes no digest policy and no other package's entry.
ownership.forbidden_paths_note: The globs **/*secret* and **/*credential* were removed. A contract catalog that models secret HANDLES must name them, and this package ships contract-catalog/shared-kernel/ctr-mod-001/examples/valid-blocked-missing-secret.json and invalid-secret-handle-shape.json -- both matching a glob this manifest declared forbidden. The contradiction was found by the run authoring WP-0A-CON-004 and confirmed: the ownership validator checks writable and read-only paths but never compares forbidden_paths against declared outputs, so nothing caught it. Replaced with extensions that carry actual key material (*.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx), which is what the rule was for. A filename is not a secret; a private key file is.

amends_without_owning.rationale: Renaming ownership.branch is pinned in two files this package does not own. test-kits/branch-identity.test.mjs holds BRANCH_OWNERSHIP, the whole branch-to-package mapping, and asserts it deepEqual against every manifest declaration -- so a package that moves its own branch MUST move that row or the suite goes red for every package at once. test-kits/integrity-manifest.json then digests that test file, and the WP-0A-A0-002 guard exits 87 on a discovered test file whose digest is stale. Both edits are structural consequences of a rename this package is entitled to make, not discretionary changes: one row and one digest move, no mapping for another package changes, and no digest policy changes.

acceptance_criteria: Every fixture is validated against its own shipped schema.json by the subset validator, and every protected constraint is killed by at least one declared fixture — a constraint no fixture can kill is documentation.
Every rule in both schemas carries an x-source naming the baseline task it comes from; no rule is present without one.
MR-004 deny-by-default is expressed in the contract: a module cannot be `ready` unless activation readiness explicitly succeeded, and a `blocked` module must record what was missing.
FP-002 is expressed in the contract: a kill switch is a platform-scope deny, and disabling write preserves historical read.
A secret handle is an opaque reference; no literal credential appears in any fixture.
Both manifests declare in untestable_by_fixture the properties a single document cannot demonstrate, rather than reading as if they were materialized.
The index still reports 4 Candidate and 10 Draft: materializing a Draft contract does not promote it.
npm run check passes on pinned Node 24.20.0 / npm 11.19.0 with skipped and todo both zero.
Every rule states whether it is sourced verbatim from a named task or is a declared inference, and every citation names the correct document section.
Each obligation has its own counterexample: a fixture that violates two rules at once tests neither independently.
required_tests: Schema conformance for both contracts via the subset validator
Deny-by-default: ready without activation, and blocked without a missing list, are both rejected
Kill switch: an allowing kill switch and a business-scope kill switch are both rejected
Write disabled without historical read is rejected
A percentage decision without its allocation, and a temporary flag without expiry and owner, are rejected
Reference and secret-handle shape checks; repository protocol, ownership, role-separation and secret-scan checks
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR; removing the two contract directories leaves no persisted data, provider state, credential, migration or customer-data effect.
open_blockers: RFC-2026-004 was recorded here as Proposed and awaiting disposition before the RFC-2026-002 manual merge. That is no longer the state of the tree: its Status line in architecture/decisions/ now reads Approved 2026-09-02, the $ref integrity guard is live, and no freeze level moved. What remains is narrower and unchanged in kind: RFC-2026-004 records that its own Limitations and Rollback stand unchanged despite the disposition, so this package still inherits them; and RFC-2026-002, itself only provisional manual control rather than native branch protection, still reserves every merge into main for the Product Owner, so nothing dispositioned here lets this package merge itself.

CTR-MOD-001 (owner A0) declares secret-handle syntax chartered to CTR-SEC-001 (owner A0+A1) with no RFC. Independent security review graded this High. A1 is a required authority and is not in this session; the conflict must be resolved by the two owners, not by this package.

This said secret_handles and the repository secret scanner "compose into zero coverage" -- independent security review had probed four handle-shaped payloads and found the only one the scanner catches is the one the schema already rejects. A1 re-measured it as disposition condition C4 (commit e7b8c4b) against 15 credential bodies the pattern admits, and scripts/scan-repository-secrets.mjs detected 12. The zero-coverage claim was false in the alarming direction, which is as wrong as understating a surface. What remains is narrower and differently shaped, and is now carried verbatim in CTR-SEC-001 x-opacity-limitation: the residual is 5 of 5 lowercase-canonical forms -- bare 32-hex, a UUID, an HMAC hex digest, a passphrase and a dotted-label password -- and the real limitation is one of REACH rather than of coverage, because the scanner walks repository files at commit time and has none over a handle in a log, an event or a job, which is the surface PT-010 is actually about. The pattern is still NOT a control and must not be cited as one; A1 must specify a handle ISSUANCE format before freeze.

This said not one of the nine catalog contracts had a fixture that killed its root required list, that CON-003 enforced it for the two contracts it owns, and that the other seven were escalated to their packages. The escalation was taken up and closed catalog-wide by WP-0A-CON-008 (merged as 963990f, PR #44). It remeasured across all fourteen contracts -- 8 of 101 root required entries isolated by a negative fixture, eight contracts isolating none -- and, rather than land 101 fixtures that can rot the same way, asserts the property generatively: test-kits/contracts/catalog-registry.test.mjs drops each declared root required key from a valid example and requires the schema to reject it by name, with a floor of 101 keys exercised so a key cannot leave a required list quietly. What remains is narrower: that guard reads schema.required at the ROOT and nowhere else. A required list nested inside a subschema is outside it, and is defended only where test-kits/contracts/schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs names one by hand -- ctr-ntf-001 deep_link.required is the single nested entry -- so nested requiredness across the catalog is still unmeasured.

The ENFORCEMENT half of FP-002 — that a narrower scope cannot override a live platform kill switch — cannot be expressed in a single decision document and is not materialized. It needs an evaluator that does not exist. The ORDER half is now enforced.

MR-002 duplicate-capability resolution and MR-003 circular-dependency blocking are registry properties across multiple manifests, and FP-003 stable allocation is an evaluator property over repeated inputs. Declared in untestable_by_fixture and NOT claimed as materialized.

The dependency range grammar (MR-003), the drain and shutdown protocol timing (MR-005), the bucket allocation algorithm (FP-003), the circuit-state machine (FP-004) and the admin APIs (MR-006, FP-006) are deliberately not inferred and remain open before freeze.

This said the package depends on WP-0A-CON-002 and WP-0A-A0-002, both unmerged. Both reached main long ago -- A0-002 at 41e47bf (PR #3) and CON-002 at 1eb31c2 (PR #4) -- as did the other two declared dependencies, WP-0A-A0-001 and WP-0A-CON-001, and this package now sits on top of all four. What remains is the inheritance, which merging a branch does not discharge: both manifests still read status in_review and still record open blockers -- 13 on CON-002 and 8 on A0-002 -- and this package still inherits every one of them, including that the test-integrity guard is a tripwire with no self-anchor (A0-002) and that CTR-PAG-001 accepts a forgeable cursor with no page-size bound (CON-002).
prefer_cross_vendor_review is not satisfied; see independence.cross_vendor_exception. Recorded as an exception, not waived.
Gate G0 remains Specification Baseline Complete / External Verification Pending; this package is restricted to reversible, synthetic-only work.
